# Best payment platform for indie SaaS developers in 2026

**Stripe vs Polar vs Dodo Payments vs Creem**

The biggest decision isn't actually the transaction fee. It's whether you want to be responsible for international tax compliance or let a Merchant of Record (MoR) handle it.

For an indie SaaS developer, these four platforms represent two different approaches\:

- **Stripe\:** Maximum control, mature payment infrastructure, and generally lower base processing fees. You remain the seller and retain tax responsibilities unless you use Managed Payments.
- **Polar, Dodo, Creem\:** Merchant of Record platforms. They handle indirect taxes such as VAT, GST, and sales tax, in exchange for higher transaction fees and some loss of control.

Here's how they compare using pricing information available in November 2026.

## 1\. Quick comparison

| Platform | Base transaction fee | Monthly fee | Merchant of Record |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Stripe | 2.9% + \$0.30 | \$0 | No |
| Polar Starter | 5% + \$0.50 | \$0 | Yes |
| Dodo Payments | 4% + \$0.40 | \$0 | Yes |
| Creem | 3.9% + \$0.40 | \$0 | Yes |


US domestic card headline rates. Additional fees, plan requirements and international surcharges apply.

## 2\. Detailed breakdown

### Stripe — maximum flexibility

![CardPaymentOptions.com – Merchant account and credit card processing reviews, ratings, and comparisons. Find the best merchant services provider for your business here.](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/ZyZx-kGJMZw-frY74Lp0ngbxxLn259SUwCVVGOs1w20aKyIMId6L9a8Lefu8zLlMx7xnfJ4MU7qPcSfFbO5tVAgdPB1Khq5kNSJbYx1vk3M83mq8t33NR3qOgnaDJXn_nY49IEKKDAg_eN4eUQrXqatPrzUusxUBWQPGwHzhUeEf4Nh96ZP9rKyCEo6DL8AI?purpose=fullsize)

**[Stripe](https://stripe.com)**

(Best for control and flexibility)

Payment processor, not automatically an MoR

Stripe remains a strong option if you're comfortable building and maintaining your own billing infrastructure.

**Advantages**

- Excellent APIs, SDKs, documentation and webhooks.
- Stripe Billing supports subscriptions, trials, metered billing and usage-based pricing.
- Stripe Checkout and Customer Portal.
- Mature fraud prevention through Radar.
- Extensive integrations and payment methods.
- Strong infrastructure for scaling beyond an indie SaaS.

**Disadvantages**

- You're responsible for tax registration, filing and remittance unless you use a separate compliance service or Managed Payments.
- Billing costs an additional 0.7% on pay-as-you-go pricing.
- International cards cost extra.
- More engineering and financial administration.

An important 2026 development: Stripe now offers **Managed Payments**, its own Merchant of Record solution. It adds 3.5% to standard Stripe processing fees and includes indirect tax compliance, fraud prevention, dispute management and global transaction support in more than 75 countries. [stripe.com](https://stripe.com/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[stripe.com](https://stripe.com/managed-payments?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**My take\:** Choose Stripe if you want complete control over your payment architecture, have mostly domestic customers, or anticipate complex billing requirements.

---

### Polar — developer-first monetization

![Polar: Open source monetization platform for developers | Product Hunt](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/0bTZF0LVIRxIKGJMdIuDNaHaZg6LA-RWSpTVp2O_taP-bblQYBPurcntoIMrzYY8DxMUYsc9upZ0pyXQ_48nNzBWVNvuorAwzSkbP2SV8Kaym3CFj1qDwDogMqXIqv_TXaix1NJFcQQe-R4F-bucQMYvQnmCS4_6LvLmPFMeR52IVFZ9n1XSHLzQABxPdtQq?purpose=fullsize)

**[Polar.sh](https://polar.sh)**

(Best for developer experience)

Open-source Merchant of Record

Polar is particularly interesting for developers selling software, APIs, developer tools and digital products.

**Advantages**

- Open-source platform.
- Modern API and SDKs.
- Built-in subscriptions and customer management.
- License keys and entitlements.
- Usage-based billing.
- GitHub-oriented monetization features.
- Handles international sales taxes as MoR.

**2026 pricing\:**

| Plan | Monthly | Transaction |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Starter | Free | 5% + \$0.50 |
| Pro | \$20 | 3.8% + \$0.40 |
| Growth | \$100 | 3.6% + \$0.35 |
| Scale | \$400 | 3.4% + \$0.30 |


Additional international card fee: 1.5%.

The paid plans become economical at approximately \$1,379, \$5,634 and \$19,048 monthly sales respectively, compared with Starter. [polar.sh](https://polar.sh/resources/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[polar.sh](https://polar.sh/blog/introducing-polar-plans?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Disadvantages**

- Starter's 5% + \$0.50 is relatively expensive.
- International card surcharges.
- Payout-provider fees.
- Younger ecosystem than Stripe.

**My take\:** If you're building a developer-focused SaaS, particularly something connected to GitHub, APIs or software licenses, Polar deserves serious consideration.

---

### Dodo Payments — global payments and emerging markets

![Dodo Payments | Krain AI](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/djvj42OhPMkoc_npTI0uhW0YfIE40Q5E2FGPIqQnD1qxkZrAoSm6T9oxkM7MJPpkDrpHIsPFzLwh1c1jYp-XOvx-vdocUvd5n6Rt7sDIj8r4jj4OnZ902VWE6sXZS4KZLUDOccJlDIlU23V_eraCrNR1xXMasj1qEUIXSRTYImVMndcRAifz9PaF8pG2TF3e?purpose=fullsize)

**[Dodo Payments](https://dodopayments.com)**

(Best to investigate for global reach)

Merchant of Record

Dodo is focused on SaaS, AI products and digital commerce.

**Advantages**

- Merchant of Record tax handling.
- No mandatory monthly platform fee.
- Subscriptions and usage-based billing.
- Local payment options.
- India-specific domestic payment pricing.
- License keys and digital product distribution.
- Tax management covering 190+ countries.

**Pricing\:**

| Transaction type | Fee |
|--------|--------|
| US cards | 4% + \$0.40 |
| International cards | Additional 1.5% |
| India domestic cards | 4% + \$0.15 |
| ACH direct debit | 1.5%, capped at \$15 |
| SEPA direct debit | 1.5%, capped at €15 |


There are additional charges for certain billing and distribution features. For example, the pricing page lists a 0.7% billing transaction charge and a \$30 dispute fee. Check which charges apply to your particular configuration. [dodopayments.com](https://dodopayments.com/pricing.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[stripe.com](https://stripe.com/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[polar.sh](https://polar.sh/resources/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.creem.io](https://www.creem.io/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Disadvantages**

- Additional costs can accumulate.
- Smaller third-party integration ecosystem.
- Dispute fees are worth considering.
- More complicated pricing than the headline 4% + \$0.40 suggests.

**My take\:** Dodo is worth investigating if your customer base is geographically diverse, particularly if you need local payment methods in India and other emerging markets.

---

### Creem — straightforward indie SaaS payments

![Creem](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/uAi-HwEu2VXddAG9Yy77YNAINxyzye4F6z971-jwz1nKHFXQhEKNYBKDq8IjWe_eWvvuqBfduUzjEz6bmu8pgUXXRg5AqvhOcLCJVnq-3z48-szmQ37Hrmq_ctQzmChKNWtnzp-ZwCfXSbk0njBwXOUiXSLb4yagANLNrUnBKhM6LEX43HRjMrIu9-yj6Xqj?purpose=fullsize)

**[Creem](https://www.creem.io)**

(Best for simple published pricing)

Merchant of Record

Creem has a particularly straightforward proposition: one published base transaction rate, with no monthly subscription or setup fee.

**Advantages**

- 3.9% + \$0.40 per successful transaction.
- No mandatory monthly fee.
- Tax collection and remittance.
- Subscription management.
- Usage-based billing and custom meters.
- Credit wallets.
- APIs, SDKs, CLI and webhooks.
- Revenue splits and affiliate functionality.
- No additional international card surcharge according to its pricing page.

**Payouts\:** Processed twice monthly, on the 1st and 15th.

**Disadvantages**

- Smaller ecosystem than Stripe.
- Some advanced capabilities have additional fees.
- Revenue splits and affiliate features have additional charges.
- Fewer established integrations.

Creem's published standard pricing includes VAT, GST and sales-tax handling in 50+ countries. Don't assume this means universal tax coverage in every jurisdiction. [www.creem.io](https://www.creem.io/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.creem.io](https://www.creem.io/blog/best-merchant-of-record-saas-2026?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**My take\:** Creem is an attractive option if you want to launch quickly without managing your own international tax infrastructure.

## 3\. What does a \$30/month SaaS subscription actually cost?

Let's compare a hypothetical \$30 subscription paid by a US customer using a domestic card.

Assumes one successful transaction, no refunds, no optional add-ons, and excludes any tax added to the customer price.

| Platform | Transaction fee | You receive |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Stripe | \$1.17 | \$28.83 |
| Polar Starter | \$2.00 | \$28.00 |
| Polar Pro | \$1.54 | \$28.46 |
| Dodo | \$1.60 | \$28.40 |
| Creem | \$1.57 | \$28.43 |

| platform | Fee |
| --- | --- |
| Stripe | 1.17 |
| Polar Starter | 2 |

| Dodo | 1.6 |
| Creem | 1.57 |


Important: Stripe's figure excludes subscription billing software and tax compliance. Adding Stripe Billing at 0.7% would add another \$0.21, and Stripe Tax Basic may add another 0.5% where applicable. Managed Payments has its own additional 3.5% fee. ## 4\. Developer experience and feature comparison

This is where the decision gets more interesting than pricing.

| Subscriptions | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Usage-based billing | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Customer portal | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| License keys | Custom | Built-in | Built-in | Built-in |
| Tax compliance | Add-on / MoR | Included | Included | Included |
| Open source | No | Yes | No | No |
| API / SDK | Excellent | Excellent | Good | Good |
| No monthly fee | Yes | Starter | Yes | Yes |


Feature-level comparison; exact availability and implementation vary by plan. Verify individual integrations and capabilities before committing.

## 5\. Which one should you choose?

My recommendations by business model\:

---

**Dodo — international customer base**

**Creem — lean indie SaaS**

Choose it if you want straightforward pricing, built-in tax handling and a relatively simple integration.

## 6\. My final recommendation

For a solo developer launching a SaaS in 2026, I'd narrow the initial evaluation to Polar and Creem.

The reasoning\:

1. You probably don't want to spend your early development time on international tax registrations and filings.
2. You probably don't need all the complexity of Stripe's payment infrastructure immediately.
3. A predictable fee structure makes it easier to calculate margins.
4. Both Polar and Creem offer developer-focused monetization features.

I'd keep Stripe in consideration if you anticipate more sophisticated billing or have plans to build a larger payments infrastructure.

One important caveat: an MoR handles transaction-related tax responsibilities within its agreement and coverage. It does not eliminate your company's own income-tax, corporate-tax or other business obligations.

Merchant of Record

Creem has a particularly straightforward proposition: one published base transaction rate, with no monthly subscription or setup fee.

**Advantages**

- 3.9% + \$0.40 per successful transaction.
- No mandatory monthly fee.
- Tax collection and remittance.
- Subscription management.
- Usage-based billing and custom meters.
- Credit wallets.
- APIs, SDKs, CLI and webhooks.
- Revenue splits and affiliate functionality.
- No additional international card surcharge according to its pricing page.

**Payouts\:** Processed twice monthly, on the 1st and 15th.

**Disadvantages**

- Smaller ecosystem than Stripe.
- Some advanced capabilities have additional fees.
- Revenue splits and affiliate features have additional charges.
- Fewer established integrations.

Creem's published standard pricing includes VAT, GST and sales-tax handling in 50+ countries. Don't assume this means universal tax coverage in every jurisdiction. ## 6\. My final recommendation

For a solo developer launching a SaaS in 2026, I'd narrow the initial evaluation to Polar and Creem.

The reasoning\:

1. You probably don't want to spend your early development time on international tax registrations and filings.
2. You probably don't need all the complexity of Stripe's payment infrastructure immediately.
3. A predictable fee structure makes it easier to calculate margins.
4. Both Polar and Creem offer developer-focused monetization features.

I'd keep Stripe in consideration if you anticipate more sophisticated billing or have plans to build a larger payments infrastructure.

One important caveat: an MoR handles transaction-related tax responsibilities within its agreement and coverage. It does not eliminate your company's own income-tax, corporate-tax or other business obligations.
